figures.caption: Overview of CVAE-BIO pipeline: pipeline of biochemical-knowledge-driven machine learning models for AMP discovery and validation. (a) Schematic workflow illustrating three core modules: Module I—Novel peptide generation from an AMP database using a CVAE model; module II—Antimicrobial activity prediction model to identify promising candidates based on a biologically informed classifier; and module III—Wet-lab validation of selected peptides. (b) Architecture of the CVAE model used in module I for peptide sequence generation. (c) the panel of 30 biochemical features incorporated in the anti-microbial activity prediction model in the module II. (d) In vitro testing of peptides prioritized from module II against clinically relevant bacterial pathogens in module III. Note: CVAE: Conditional variational autoencoder. AMP: Antimicrobial peptides. The green arrows in Fig. 1a and Fig. 1b represent the training process, and the orange arrows represent the data inputting/outputting process.
figures.label: Figure 1

figures.caption: Model performance comparison for AMP activity prediction model selection in module II. (a) ROC evaluating classifier performance on the held-out test set. (b) PR curves of classifying active peptides in the held-out testing set. Note: CNN_BERT: Convolutional neural network trained on contextualized language model embeddings generated by BERT (bidirectional encoder representations from transformers). RF_BERT: Random Forest classifier trained on BERT-based embeddings. CNN_T5: Convolutional neural network trained on T5 derived embeddings. RF_T5: Random Forest classifier trained on unidirectional T5 embeddings. RF_Bio: Random forest classifier trained on the panel of 30 biochemical features. SVM_Bio: Support vector machine trained on the panel of 30 biochemical features. HydrAMP-classifier: LSTM-based (long short-term memory) recurrent neural network model specifically developed for AMP prediction. AUROC: Area under the ROC curve. AUPRC: Area under the precision-recall curve.
figures.label: Figure 2

figures.caption: UMAP embedding and clustering analysis of peptide SHAP values from biochemical feature-based RF activity prediction, and cluster-specific feature importance and feature values. (a) SHAP-based clustering of the training set in 2D UMAP space. (b) SHAP-based clustering of the held-out test set in 2D UMAP space. (c) Cluster-wise dot plot of scaled mean SHAP values for features positively contributing to MIC ≤ 10 μg/mL classification. (d) Cluster-wise dot plot of scaled mean SHAP values for features negatively contributing to MIC ≤ 10 μg/mL classification. Note: MIC: Minimum inhibitory concentration. In panels (a) and (b), SHAP values for peptides in the training set and the held-out test set were embedded in 2-dimentioanl UMAP space respectively with actual activity labels (MIC ≤ 10 μg/mL: Active; MIC > 10 μg/mL: Inactive), and clustered by KMeans clustering (k = 6). Voronoi boundaries indicates KMeans clustering boundaries performed in UMAP space. In panels (c) and (d), each dot encodes scaled feature importance (dot size) and mean scaled feature value. Scaled importance is calculated as the mean SHAP value weighted by the proportion of peptides with non-zero contributions.
figures.label: Figure 3

figures.caption: In vitro activity and toxicity validation of all 54 CVAE-BIO–generated peptides. (a) Antibacterial activity against E. Coli ATCC 25922 at 50 μg/mL and at 10 μg/mL. (b) Hemolysis of human erythrocytes at 50 μg/mL. Note: Relative growth ratio: Relative growth ratios in the bar plot are normalized measures of how much the bacteria grew in the presence of a peptide, relative to an untreated growth control (no peptide) in the same assay. The two dashed lines indicate 10% hemolysis and 5% hemolysis, which were used as reference thresholds to assess antibacterial activity.

figures.caption: In vitro antimicrobial activity of CVAE-BIO–generated peptides against E. Coli and S. Aureus at 50 μg/mL, and against ESKAPE bacterial strains at 10 μg/mL and 10% Hemolysis of human erythrocytes at 50 μg/mL. Note: ESKAPE: ESKAPE is an acronym comprising the scientific names of six highly virulent and antibiotic resistant bacterial pathogens including: Enterococcus spp, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Enterobacter spp. The leftmost to the ninth columns of blocks indicate observable bacterial growth inhibition at the respective concentration. The rightmost column of blocks indicate observable hemolysis at or below the 10% hemolysis threshold.

figures.caption: Comparison of biochemical feature distributions among the CVAE-BIO-generated peptides and APD3 peptides. (a–h) Distributions of peptide length, net charge, Boman index, instability index, isoelectric point, hydrophobic moment (100°), hydrophobicity, and percentage of charged residues for CVAE-BIO-generated peptides compared to APD3 peptides. (i–j) Counts of tiny residues in the complete set of CVAE-BIO-generated and APD3 peptides, as well as in subsets of CVAE-BIO peptides stratified by antimicrobial activity: MIC ≤10 μg/mL, 10 μg/mL < MIC ≤50 μg/mL, and MIC >50 μg/mL. (k-l) Corresponding distributions of small residue counts across the same peptide groups as in (i–j). A marked reduction in tiny and small residue content is observed in CVAE-BIO-generated peptides with MIC ≤10 μg/mL. Note: MIC: Minimum inhibitory concentration. Statistical significance was assessed using the Mann–Whitney U test.
